title: Build end-to-end accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA, canvas semantics, inclusive design)
body:
## Context

Accessibility is LOCKED DECISION 10 (CLAUDE.md §2): **WCAG 2.2 AA on every platform** (iPadOS, Android, Web), platform screen readers for all chrome, and OCR-backed alt-text for handwriting. It is a **build gate, not a phase** — `docs/design/accessibility.md` states a surface is not done until it passes the criteria there. The hard part is that the ink canvas is a bitmap/vector surface that is **opaque to assistive technology**, so we must build a **parallel accessible model** on top of the canvas on every platform (`accessibility.md` §3; PRD-CO-330). This is also a market wedge: no ink app exposes handwriting to screen readers well (`prd-04` §8, user-pain idea #20), and Sane can because it OCRs on-device. This epic delivers semantics for all chrome, the parallel canvas tree, Dynamic Type, reduce-motion, OS display-setting adaptation, keyboard/switch/voice operability, non-gesture alternatives, colour-blind and motor-assist inclusive features, captions, automated a11y tests, and the pre-beta audit + Apple Accessibility Nutrition Labels. Accessibility is cross-cutting — built alongside the editor (M1) and every surface it grows into — and **formally audited in M7 Beta Hardening & Security Audit** ({{SN-A11Y-017}}). Grounding: `docs/design/accessibility.md` (primary), `docs/product/prd-04-sharing-collaboration-ai-study-a11y-i18n.md` §8 (PRD-CO-310–339), `docs/design/gestures-and-shortcuts.md` (non-gesture alternatives), `docs/design/design-system.md` + `docs/design/tokens.json` (contrast/tokens), `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` (per-screen mapping).

## Scope

**In:** the whole accessibility programme across `app/`, `packages/sane_ui`, and the ink/audio/OCR feature packages — chrome semantics, the parallel canvas a11y tree, text scaling, reduce-motion, OS display-setting adaptation, keyboard/focus, non-gesture alternatives, Switch/Voice support, colour-blind palette + names, left-handed mode, motor assist, reading mode, audio captions, the automated a11y test harness, and the pre-beta audit + store labels.

**Out:** the a11y-adjusted contrast token derivation and its CI floor (owned by the design system: SN-DS-006 and SN-DS-007) — this epic consumes them; the raw ink stabilisation filter (SN-INK-003) — this epic exposes its presets; localisation/RTL mechanics beyond how left-handed composes with them (owned by SN-I18N-001).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every child issue below is merged, CI green, and its own acceptance criteria met.
- [ ] Body text meets 4.5:1 and large/UI/focus 3:1 in every look x mode (via SN-DS-006 adjusted tokens); text scales to 200% and reflows at 320 CSS px; no colour-only information; targets meet 44 pt / 48 dp / 24 px.
- [ ] Every path gesture and drag has a documented non-gesture alternative; full keyboard operability with no traps; visible focus never obscured.
- [ ] The ink canvas publishes a parallel accessible tree verified with VoiceOver, TalkBack and NVDA/JAWS end-to-end for a common-task flow.
- [ ] The eight Apple Accessibility Nutrition Label features are truthfully declarable and the Play pre-launch accessibility report is clean ({{SN-A11Y-017}}).

## Children

- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-002}} Expose Semantics for all app chrome
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-003}} Parallel accessible canvas tree for note objects
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-004}} OCR-transcript object descriptions + custom actions
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-005}} Dynamic Type, 200% scaling and text-spacing overrides
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-006}} Honour Reduce Motion across every animation
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-007}} Adapt to OS contrast / transparency / colour settings
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-008}} Keyboard navigation and focus order (web/desktop)
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-009}} Non-gesture and non-drag alternatives for every interaction
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-010}} Switch Control and Voice Control support
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-011}} Colour-blind-safe ink palette, preview and colour names
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-012}} Left-handed mode composing with RTL
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-013}} Motor assist: stabilisation presets, larger targets, single-touch
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-014}} Reading mode with Read Aloud and dyslexia fonts
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-015}} Captions and searchable transcripts for audio
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-016}} Automated accessibility tests (semantics, contrast, axe)
- [ ] {{SN-A11Y-017}} Pre-beta accessibility audit + nutrition labels

## Technical notes

Flutter `Semantics` / `CustomPaint.semanticsBuilder` is the single mechanism projecting to VoiceOver, TalkBack and web ARIA (`accessibility.md` §1). Chrome semantics live in `packages/sane_ui` components and `app/` screens; the canvas tree lives with the editor (`app/lib/editor/**`, consuming `sane_core` object model). Honour `MediaQuery` accessibility flags (`textScaler`, `disableAnimations`, `highContrast`, `boldText`, `accessibleNavigation`) and platform channels for settings Flutter does not surface. Follows ADR-0003 (state/app structure) and the design-system codegen (SN-DS-002/006/007). Flutter web semantics is historically the weakest surface and MUST be tested explicitly ({{SN-A11Y-016}}).

## Security & privacy

Accessible descriptions surface **user note content** (OCR transcripts, object labels, captions) to the platform a11y APIs on-device; this content MUST never be logged (CWE-532, MASVS-PRIVACY-3) and MUST never leave the device to be described or read aloud — OCR/TTS run on-device (MASVS-PRIVACY-2, MASVS-NETWORK-1). Correct platform a11y integration is what lets us declare labels truthfully (MASVS-PLATFORM-1). No new network egress is introduced by any child.

## UX notes

Delivers the inclusive half of every screen proven in `design/Sane Notes.dc.html` (Login, Profiles, Onboarding, Library, Editor, Templates, Share, Import, Upgrade, Search, Settings) per the per-screen mapping in `accessibility.md` §10, across all 17 looks + dark mode. Voice is warm and honest (`design-system.md` §1) — a11y affordances (Convert to text, larger targets, colour names) read as first-class features, not compliance bolt-ons.

## Test plan

Each child names its own tests. Epic-level gates: the automated a11y harness ({{SN-A11Y-016}}: `flutter_test` semantics + contrast + axe on web) and the manual multi-screen-reader audit ({{SN-A11Y-017}}).

## Dependencies

SN-DS-002 (tokens/ThemeExtension) and SN-DS-003 (core components) for chrome; SN-ED-002 (editor canvas) and SN-CORE-002 (object model) for the canvas tree; SN-HWR-001 (OCR) for object descriptions and reading mode; SN-AUD-002 (recorder) for captions. Children carry finer-grained `depends_on`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Expose Semantics for all app chrome (name, role, state, value)
body:
## Context

WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) requires that **every custom-drawn control exposes name/role/state/value** to the platform a11y API (`accessibility.md` §2, PRD-CO-321). Sane's chrome is built from custom `sane_ui` widgets (palette dock, page rail, chips, segmented controls, toggles, share roles), not native controls, so nothing is accessible unless we attach `Semantics` explicitly. This issue establishes the semantics conventions and applies them to the shell and editor chrome that ship in M1, with the same conventions reused as Library, Templates, Share, Search and Settings chrome land in later milestones (per-screen requirements in `accessibility.md` §10). Without it, VoiceOver/TalkBack/NVDA read blank or wrong labels and the app fails the store nutrition labels.

## Scope

**In:** a documented semantics convention (label/role/state/value/hint patterns) baked into `sane_ui` components — buttons, icon buttons, chips, segmented controls, toggles, sliders, list rows, tabs, nav items; the editor toolbar (Undo announces disabled when the stack is empty; Bookmark filled/empty), the tool palette (each tool a button with selected state; colour dots labelled by **name**; width dots labelled S/M/L), the page rail (thumbnails as a list, item 'page 3 of 12, bookmarked'); `MergeSemantics` for icon+label clusters, `ExcludeSemantics`/`BlockSemantics` for decorative art; `SemanticsService.announce` for toasts mirrored to a live region (`accessibility.md` §3.3).

**Out:** the parallel **canvas object** tree ({{SN-A11Y-003}}) and OCR descriptions ({{SN-A11Y-004}}); keyboard focus order ({{SN-A11Y-008}}); the automated semantics tests ({{SN-A11Y-016}}) — this issue's own widget tests assert labels, the suite generalises them.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every interactive `sane_ui` component exposes a non-empty accessible name, correct role (button/checkbox/radio/slider/tab), and state (selected/disabled/checked/expanded) and value where applicable.
- [ ] Toolbar Undo/Redo announce their disabled state when the op-log stack is empty; Bookmark toggle announces filled/empty; Pro-gated actions announce 'Pro'.
- [ ] Colour swatches announce the colour **name** (not hex) plus selected state; width dots announce S/M/L; the visual uppercase of `label`-role text never leaks into the accessible name (original casing).
- [ ] Decorative art (login art panel, avatar colour, marketing pills) is excluded from AT via `ExcludeSemantics`.
- [ ] Toasts are announced politely via `SemanticsService.announce` and are non-interruptive.
- [ ] Verified with VoiceOver, TalkBack and NVDA that each M1 chrome control reads correctly.

## Technical notes

Use Flutter `Semantics` widgets and the `SemanticsProperties` fields (`button`, `selected`, `enabled`, `toggled`, `slider`, `value`, `hint`); reuse them inside `sane_ui` so screens do not re-wire semantics per instance. Colour names come from the ink palette naming table (feeds {{SN-A11Y-011}}). Announcements map to the design's toasts (`screens-and-flows.md` §16). Follows ADR-0003; components from `docs/design/component-inventory.md` §9 (states every component must handle). Do not use the deprecated web canvas hit-regions.

## Security & privacy

Accessible names for note-bearing chrome (a notebook title, a search snippet) are **user content** and MUST NOT be logged (CWE-532, MASVS-PRIVACY-3). Correct semantics is a platform-integration control (MASVS-PLATFORM-1). No egress; no secrets.

## UX notes

Covers the Editor chrome (`accessibility.md` §10 'the hard screen') plus the shell; every look x dark mode must keep the same semantics (semantics are look-independent, but focus rings must stay >= 3:1 — see SN-DS-006). Targets: tool buttons 44, chrome 42, chips 34 — verify chips meet the platform floor with spacing (§2 SC 2.5.8).

## Test plan

Widget/semantics: `app/test/a11y/chrome_semantics_test.dart` and `packages/sane_ui/test/a11y/component_semantics_test.dart` using `SemanticsTester`/`matchesSemantics` to assert name/role/state per component and editor control; a test asserts uppercase `label` roles expose original casing. Manual: VoiceOver/TalkBack/NVDA smoke on the editor.

## Dependencies

SN-DS-003 (core components), SN-ED-002 (editor canvas + toolbar).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Build the parallel accessible canvas tree for note objects
body:
## Context

The ink canvas is opaque to assistive technology, so each drawn object must become an addressable a11y node in a **parallel tree** kept in sync with the document model (`accessibility.md` §3, PRD-CO-330). Flutter `CustomPaint.semanticsBuilder` emits a `CustomPainterSemantics` per object (rect + label + actions) and is the single implementation projecting to iOS `UIAccessibilityElement`, Android `ExploreByTouchHelper` and web ARIA. This issue builds the tree infrastructure over the object model (strokes/stroke-groups, shapes, images, text blocks, audio anchors, comments) once shapes/images/text exist in M2; decorative ink is excluded, and transient events are announced. It is the backbone that makes handwriting navigable by screen reader — a differentiator no ink competitor delivers.

## Scope

**In:** a `semanticsBuilder` over the editor `CustomPaint` that produces one `CustomPainterSemantics` per note object with its rect (`accessibilityFrameInContainerSpace` equivalent), a label, a role/traits, and a custom-action set stub; grouping strokes into semantic **stroke groups**; `ExcludeSemantics`/null for decorative strokes (doodles, dividers) flagged in the model; `SemanticsService.announce` for transient events ('Saved', 'Deleted N strokes', 'Page 3 of 12', 'Link copied'); keeping the tree in sync incrementally as objects are added/moved/deleted without rebuilding the whole tree each frame; a page-level node exposing 'title, page X of Y'.

**Out:** the OCR transcript **content** of a handwriting block and object-type navigation ({{SN-A11Y-004}}); audio-anchor play action and captions ({{SN-A11Y-015}}); keyboard object navigation/nudge ({{SN-A11Y-008}}, {{SN-A11Y-009}}); native-only rotor plumbing if Flutter's projection proves insufficient (spike inside {{SN-A11Y-004}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each non-decorative object exposes a focusable a11y node with a correct rect that tracks pan/zoom; decorative strokes are absent from the tree.
- [ ] A shape announces its recognised name + colour name ('green rectangle'); an image announces its alt text (never 'image'); a text block announces its text.
- [ ] The page node announces 'title, page X of Y'; navigating objects with a screen reader visits them in a stable reading order (top-to-bottom, left-to-right).
- [ ] Adding/moving/deleting an object updates the tree within one frame and posts the correct change announcement; no per-frame full rebuild on the hot draw path (CLAUDE.md §8).
- [ ] VoiceOver and TalkBack can focus each object; the web parallel semantics is present and tested explicitly (Flutter web is the weakest surface, §3.1).

## Technical notes

Implement in `app/lib/editor/a11y/canvas_semantics.dart` feeding the editor `CustomPaint.semanticsBuilder`; read the object list from the `sane_core` document model (SN-CORE-002) and the decorative flag from the object metadata. Do not hop isolates on `PointerMoveEvent`; build/patch the tree on commit/idle, not during an active stroke (CLAUDE.md §8). Decorative exclusion and transient announcements per `accessibility.md` §3.2/§3.3. Custom actions are declared here as an empty extensible set that {{SN-A11Y-004}} fills.

## Security & privacy

Object labels are **user content** surfaced to AT on-device only; never log them (CWE-532, MASVS-PRIVACY-3) and never send them off-device to be generated (MASVS-PRIVACY-2, MASVS-NETWORK-1). On web the parallel semantics DOM is local to the viewer's device (no persistence, no egress). Correct projection is a platform control (MASVS-PLATFORM-1).

## UX notes

Mirrors `accessibility.md` §3.2 ('what each object announces'); the whole page carries an `aria-describedby`/`accessibilityValue` transcript summary. Works across every look/dark mode (semantics are look-independent). Reduce-motion still applies to any focus-scroll animation ({{SN-A11Y-006}}).

## Test plan

Widget/semantics: `app/test/a11y/canvas_semantics_test.dart` builds a page of mixed objects and asserts node count, rects, labels, decorative exclusion, and change announcements on add/move/delete; a web-semantics test (`flutter test --platform chrome`) asserts the tree renders on web. Manual: VoiceOver + TalkBack object navigation on a real page.

## Dependencies

SN-ED-002 (editor canvas/CustomPaint), SN-CORE-002 (object model).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Describe canvas objects with on-device OCR transcripts and custom actions
body:
## Context

WCAG 1.1.1 requires a text alternative for non-text content. A handwriting block's alternative is its **OCR transcript** ('Standing wave: two waves, same frequency...') used as the a11y label, with a `convert-to-text` custom action so a screen-reader user can act on it (`accessibility.md` §3.2, PRD-CO-310/PRD-CO-330). This is the market wedge — an ink app that reads handwriting aloud — and it depends on the on-device recognition pipeline (SN-HWR-001, ML Kit Digital Ink primary, Vision OCR fallback on iOS). This issue fills the object nodes created by {{SN-A11Y-003}} with real descriptions and the custom-action set, and adds object-type navigation (a rotor-equivalent) so users can jump between headings, images and handwriting blocks.

## Scope

**In:** wiring each handwriting stroke-group node's label to its on-device OCR transcript (user-editable so a mis-recognition can be corrected), each image node's label to its user/AI alt text, each shape to its recognised name + colour name; the custom-action set on every object node (delete, duplicate, change colour, bring-to-front, and **convert-to-text** for handwriting) exposed as `UIAccessibilityCustomAction`/Android custom `AccessibilityAction`/Flutter `CustomSemanticsAction`; an object-type navigation affordance (custom rotor on iOS via a platform channel, and an equivalent 'jump to next heading/image/handwriting' custom action on Android/web) per §3.1; announcing 'Converted to text' on completion.

**Out:** the tree infrastructure itself ({{SN-A11Y-003}}); the recognition engine ({{SN-HWR-001}}); audio anchors/captions ({{SN-A11Y-015}}); reading mode ({{SN-A11Y-014}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A handwriting block reads its OCR transcript as its accessible label; if recognition is low-confidence the label notes it and the transcript is editable inline (ink is never destroyed).
- [ ] Every object node exposes the custom actions delete/duplicate/change-colour/bring-to-front; handwriting also exposes convert-to-text, and invoking it inserts editable text and announces 'Converted to text'.
- [ ] An image with no alt text still never announces bare 'image' — it announces user or AI alt text, or a prompt to add one.
- [ ] Object-type navigation lets a VoiceOver rotor (or the Android/web equivalent action) step through headings, images and handwriting blocks.
- [ ] All recognition runs on-device (airplane-mode works); no transcript leaves the device to be generated.

## Technical notes

Consume `sane_ml`/`sane_search` OCR output (SN-HWR-001) attached to stroke groups; expose `CustomSemanticsAction`s on the `CustomPainterSemantics` from {{SN-A11Y-003}}. The iOS custom rotor and PencilKit's lack of stroke descriptions require a small platform channel (`plugins/sane_ml_native` or a dedicated a11y channel) — spike whether Flutter `CustomSemanticsAction` + the projected tree is sufficient before adding native code. OCR language selection is per-notebook (roadmap M3 exit criteria). References `accessibility.md` §3.1/§3.2/§11 and ADR-0016 (on-device ML).

## Security & privacy

OCR transcripts are **derived user content**; they MUST be generated on-device (MASVS-PRIVACY-2, MASVS-NETWORK-1 — no cloud OCR without the explicit per-request opt-in that this a11y path never takes), never logged (CWE-532, MASVS-PRIVACY-3), and honour the Settings 'On-device handwriting recognition' switch. Convert-to-text output is inserted as owned, undoable content (PRD-CO-158). Platform a11y correctness: MASVS-PLATFORM-1.

## UX notes

Matches the Editor a11y requirements (`accessibility.md` §10) and the on-device recognition toggle (Settings §12). Convert-to-text is a first-class action for all users, surfaced identically in the Selection bar and as a screen-reader custom action. Announcements follow §3.3; works across all looks/dark mode.

## Test plan

Widget/semantics: `app/test/a11y/object_descriptions_test.dart` asserts transcript labels, the custom-action set, convert-to-text insertion + announcement, and image alt-text fallback; a fake on-device OCR provider drives deterministic transcripts. Negative: an offline (airplane-mode simulated) run still produces labels. Manual: VoiceOver rotor object-type jump on a mixed page.

## Dependencies

{{SN-A11Y-003}} (canvas tree), SN-HWR-001 (on-device OCR/recognition).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Support Dynamic Type, 200% text scaling and text-spacing overrides
body:
## Context

WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text), 1.4.10 (Reflow) and 1.4.12 (Text Spacing) require that chrome text scales to 200% without loss, reflows at 320 CSS px with no 2-D scroll, and tolerates spacing overrides (line 1.5x, para 2x, letter 0.12x, word 0.16x) without clipping (`accessibility.md` §7, PRD-CO-313/PRD-CO-314). The fixed type scale in `tokens.json` is in px; the client MUST apply the OS scale factor on top via `MediaQuery.textScaler` (iOS `UIFontMetrics`, Android `sp`). `SaneText` (design system) applies the scaler; this issue makes the **app-level layout** survive it — no fixed heights that clip, palettes/dialogs reflow, and every overlay stays usable at 320 px + 200%. Students on cheap phones and older readers depend on this.

## Scope

**In:** an app-wide audit + fixes ensuring chrome uses min/preferred sizing (not fixed heights that clip scaled text); the editor toolbar/palette dock, page rail, sidebar, and dialogs reflow and remain operable at 200% text and 320 CSS px; overlays (as each ships: Templates, Import, Share, Upgrade, Search, Settings) remain fully usable at 320 px + 200%; a global text-spacing tolerance pass (line-height 1.5x etc. cause no truncation); honouring iPad Dynamic Type up to ~140% and general OS scaling; a reusable `AccessibleScaffold`/layout helper if needed so screens inherit correct scaling behaviour.

**Out:** the `SaneText` role widget and `textScaler` plumbing (SN-DS-010, design system); the reading-mode font picker + Read Aloud ({{SN-A11Y-014}}); localisation string expansion (SN-I18N-001, though this pass must not regress it).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All chrome text scales to 200% via `MediaQuery.textScaler` with no clipping, overlap, or lost controls; no widget hard-codes a height that truncates scaled text.
- [ ] At 320 CSS px width the editor and each shipped overlay reflow to a single column with no horizontal scroll (tables/diagrams/code excepted, each in their own scroll container).
- [ ] Applying the 1.4.12 spacing overrides (line 1.5x, para 2x, letter 0.12x, word 0.16x) shows no truncation in chrome, typed blocks, or OCR transcripts.
- [ ] iPad honours Dynamic Type to at least ~140%; Android respects `sp`; web respects browser zoom to 200%.
- [ ] A CI check renders key screens at `textScaler` 2.0 and 320 px and fails on overflow.

## Technical notes

Use `MediaQuery.textScalerOf(context)` and `LayoutBuilder`/`Flexible`/`Wrap` instead of fixed extents; clamp only where a control must stay tappable. Reflow follows the design `narrow` (< 900 px) collapse rules (`screens-and-flows.md`); the sidebar collapses, palettes re-dock. Golden/overflow assertions can use `debugAssertAllRenderVarsUnset`-style overflow detection or a golden at scaled sizes. References `accessibility.md` §7 and `design-system.md` §3 (fixed scale, family swaps). Compose with RTL and left-handed later ({{SN-A11Y-012}}).

## Security & privacy

None beyond baseline: layout only; the widget renders user strings (titles, transcripts) and MUST NOT log them (CWE-532). Correct platform text-scaling integration: MASVS-PLATFORM-1. No egress, no storage, no secrets.

## UX notes

Type sizes are fixed per role and only the family swaps per look (`design-system.md` §3), so scaling is uniform across all 17 looks + dark mode. The greeting/headings must not overrun their surfaces at max scale; the palette dock stays reachable. This underpins the Apple 'Larger Text (200%+)' nutrition label ({{SN-A11Y-017}}).

## Test plan

Widget/golden: `app/test/a11y/text_scaling_test.dart` pumps the editor + each shipped overlay at `textScaler` 1.0/1.5/2.0 and at 320/400/820 px widths, asserting no `RenderFlex` overflow and that key controls remain hit-testable; a spacing-override case applies the 1.4.12 multipliers. Manual: iPad Dynamic Type slider, Android font-size, browser zoom smoke.

## Dependencies

SN-DS-003 (components render via SaneText/textScaler).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Honour Reduce Motion across every animation
body:
## Context

WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions) is treated as **required** for Sane (`accessibility.md` §6, §2 table; PRD-CO-317): when the OS Reduce Motion setting is on (iOS `UIAccessibility.isReduceMotionEnabled`, Android remove-animations, web `prefers-reduced-motion`) all interaction motion must be replaced by cross-fades or removed, and functional state changes must remain visible without motion. This lets us **truthfully declare 'Reduced Motion'** in the Apple Accessibility Nutrition Label. It also matters for vestibular-disorder users and for LOCKED DECISION 10. The design's motion tokens live in the design system (SN-DS-025); this issue enforces the reduce-motion policy app-wide and pins the functional-vs-decorative motion rules.

## Scope

**In:** reading the OS reduce-motion flag via `MediaQuery.of(context).disableAnimations` (and platform channel where needed) and a single `SaneMotion` policy that: replaces directional/scale transitions (overlay slide, page turn, zoom) with **cross-fades**; **disables** decorative motion (brush fly-ins, audio-bar flourish, dock edge-glow pulse); converts the recording indicator to a **steady red dot + 'Recording' label** (never a pulse, so motion is never the only signal, 1.4.1/2.3.3); reduces ink-replay dimming to an instant reveal; shortens any remaining essential motion under the interaction thresholds; ensuring nothing flashes > 3x/s (2.3.1).

**Out:** the motion token/duration definitions (SN-DS-025, design system) — this consumes them; the wallpaper/glass contrast handling ({{SN-A11Y-007}}); specific per-feature animations owned by their feature epics (this issue provides the policy + gate they must use).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With Reduce Motion on, every overlay/page-turn/zoom transition becomes a cross-fade or is removed; no slide/scale motion plays.
- [ ] The recording indicator stops pulsing and shows a steady dot + 'Recording' text; audio-bar flourish and dock edge-glow do not animate.
- [ ] Nothing in the app flashes more than 3 times per second in either motion mode.
- [ ] Ink replay under Reduce Motion reveals instantly rather than animating the playhead dim.
- [ ] A lint/test gate flags any `AnimationController`/implicit animation that does not consult the `SaneMotion` policy.

## Technical notes

Centralise in `packages/sane_ui/lib/src/motion/` (or `app/` if it coordinates features): a `SaneMotion.reduced(context)` helper and reduced variants of the shared transitions; feed `PageTransitionsTheme`/route builders through it. Consume durations from SN-DS-025. Recording-dot behaviour references `accessibility.md` §6 and the audio spec. `disableAnimations` is the cross-platform signal; verify web `prefers-reduced-motion` maps through Flutter web. Do not animate on the hot draw path regardless of the setting (CLAUDE.md §8).

## Security & privacy

None beyond baseline: motion policy only; no content is logged (CWE-532), no egress, no secrets. Correct platform-setting integration is a platform control (MASVS-PLATFORM-1) and underpins a truthful store label.

## UX notes

Applies across all 17 looks + dark mode; the reduced variants must still communicate the same state (a functional change is shown statically, never dropped). Motion durations and the reduce-motion mapping are documented in `ux-principles.md` §6. The steady recording dot must keep >= 3:1 non-text contrast (1.4.11).

## Test plan

Widget: `app/test/a11y/reduce_motion_test.dart` pumps with `MediaQueryData(disableAnimations: true)` and asserts transitions resolve to cross-fade/none, the recording indicator is static with a text label, and no animation exceeds thresholds; a gate test greps for animation APIs bypassing `SaneMotion`. Manual: toggle Reduce Motion on iOS/Android/Chrome and observe overlays + recording.

## Dependencies

SN-DS-003 (components/transitions); consumes SN-DS-025 (motion tokens).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Adapt to OS contrast, transparency and colour display settings
body:
## Context

Beyond the baseline AA contrast the design tokens guarantee (derived by SN-DS-006 and gated by SN-DS-007), Sane must **adapt to OS accessibility display settings**: Increase/Darker Contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Bold Text, Reduce Transparency on iOS, and colour correction/inversion + high-contrast on Android, plus web `prefers-contrast` (`accessibility.md` §4.2, PRD-CO-334). Wallpaper/glass looks turn surfaces 84% translucent, which can drop chrome-text contrast below AA, so the veil must be clamped. This issue provides a high-contrast variant and the transparency clamp so users who need more contrast get it without leaving their chosen look.

## Scope

**In:** reading `MediaQuery` `highContrast`/`boldText` and platform-channel signals for Reduce Transparency / Differentiate Without Color / colour inversion; a **high-contrast variant** that, when requested, bumps borders to `--ink`, removes translucency, and raises `mu` toward `ink`; a **transparency clamp** in wallpaper/glass mode that increases surface opacity or adds a scrim so chrome text never drops below 4.5:1 (the veil slider cannot push contrast below AA); honouring Bold Text by increasing font weight where the look allows; ensuring Differentiate Without Color pairs every colour signal with a non-colour cue (delegating detail to {{SN-A11Y-011}}).

**Out:** the base per-look token derivation and CI floor (SN-DS-006 / SN-DS-007); the colour-blind ink palette + names ({{SN-A11Y-011}}); reduce-motion ({{SN-A11Y-006}}).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With Increase/High Contrast on, borders become `--ink`, translucency is removed, and `mu` is raised so all chrome text meets >= 4.5:1 and UI components >= 3:1 in every look x mode.
- [ ] In wallpaper/glass mode the effective chrome-text contrast is clamped to >= 4.5:1 regardless of veil-slider position and wallpaper choice (re-verified over each `WALLS` preset).
- [ ] Reduce Transparency (iOS) / equivalent removes backdrop blur and makes `sf`/`sf2` opaque.
- [ ] Bold Text increases weight without clipping (composes with {{SN-A11Y-005}} scaling).
- [ ] Colour inversion / colour-correction on Android does not corrupt the ink canvas colours (canvas exempt from chrome contrast; user drawing preserved).

## Technical notes

Read `MediaQuery.of(context).highContrast`/`boldText`; add a platform channel (`plugins/` a11y channel) for Reduce Transparency, Differentiate Without Color, and Smart/Colour Invert where Flutter does not surface them. Select a high-contrast token overlay in `SaneLook` (extends SN-DS-002/006). The wallpaper clamp lives with the wallpaper surface mode (SN-DS-014); compute effective contrast over the frosted surface composited on the blurred wallpaper (WCAG sRGB formula). The ink canvas is exempt from chrome contrast rules (`accessibility.md` §4.2) but must not be smart-inverted. References `accessibility.md` §4.2.

## Security & privacy

None beyond baseline: display adaptation over design tokens; no content logging (CWE-532), no egress. Correct platform-setting integration (MASVS-PLATFORM-1) underpins the truthful 'Sufficient Contrast' and 'Differentiate Without Color' store labels ({{SN-A11Y-017}}).

## UX notes

Users keep their chosen look while gaining contrast; low-contrast-accent looks (Cyberpunk, Neo-Brutalism light) fall back to the adjusted accent or `--ink` for focus rings and icons (SN-DS-006). Verify across all 17 looks + dark mode, especially Glass/Y2K translucency and Cyberpunk neon. Toast (the only inverted surface) is re-verified for Cyberpunk/Glass.

## Test plan

Widget/unit: `app/test/a11y/os_display_settings_test.dart` pumps with `highContrast: true` / `boldText: true` and a faked reduce-transparency channel, asserting opaque surfaces, `--ink` borders, and computed contrast >= 4.5 across a sample of looks; `packages/sane_ui/test/a11y/wallpaper_contrast_test.dart` asserts the clamp holds over every `WALLS` preset at extreme veil. Manual: iOS Increase Contrast / Reduce Transparency; Android colour inversion.

## Dependencies

SN-DS-002 (tokens/ThemeExtension); consumes SN-DS-006 (adjusted tokens) and SN-DS-014 (wallpaper surface mode).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Implement keyboard navigation and focus order for web and desktop
body:
## Context

Full keyboard operability (WCAG 2.1.1) is required and is the backbone of Switch and Voice access (`accessibility.md` §8, PRD-CO-315/PRD-CO-316). Tab order must follow visual order, focus must be visible on every control (2.4.7) and never fully obscured by the sticky toolbar/floating palette/page rail (2.4.11), with no keyboard traps (2.1.2). A hardware keyboard is first-class on web/desktop and on tablets with a keyboard (`gestures-and-shortcuts.md` §6). Freehand drawing itself is exempt as an essential analog gesture, but **choosing tools and placing/editing objects must be keyboard-operable**. This issue delivers the focus system, the shortcut map, skip links/landmarks, and canvas object navigation by keyboard.

## Scope

**In:** a `FocusTraversalOrder` matching visual order across the shell + editor; a visible focus ring (>= 2 px, >= 3:1) on every control that is never fully hidden by the dock/rail/overlays; no traps; the keyboard shortcut map from `gestures-and-shortcuts.md` §6 (tool single-keys P/H/E/V/S/T/I/R suppressed while a text field is focused; `Cmd/Ctrl` edit/file/nav shortcuts; `Esc` returns focus to canvas / cancels; `Cmd//` cheat sheet); skip links / ARIA landmarks on web (skip to canvas, skip to sidebar; landmarks for sidebar/main/toolbar); **canvas object navigation** via a roving-tabindex or 'canvas objects' landmark so a keyboard user steps through the parallel a11y-tree objects, with arrow keys nudging a selected object and Enter/Space activating.

**Out:** the non-drag numeric-entry alternatives for resize/reorder/colour ({{SN-A11Y-009}}); Switch/Voice mapping ({{SN-A11Y-010}}); the canvas semantics tree itself ({{SN-A11Y-003}}); text-box formatting shortcuts (owned by SN-TXT-001, referenced here for suppression rules).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every function except raw inking is reachable by keyboard; Tab visits controls in visual order; Shift+Tab reverses; no element traps focus.
- [ ] A visible focus indicator (>= 2 px, >= 3:1 focused vs unfocused) shows on every control and is never fully obscured by the palette dock, page rail, audio bar, or an overlay.
- [ ] The documented shortcuts perform their action; single-key tool switches type characters (do not switch tools) while a text field is focused; `Esc` cancels/returns to canvas; `Cmd//` shows the cheat sheet.
- [ ] On web, skip links and ARIA landmarks (sidebar/main/toolbar) are present and a screen-reader user can skip to canvas or sidebar.
- [ ] A keyboard user can step through canvas objects (roving tabindex), nudge a selected object with arrow keys, and activate with Enter/Space, with focus never trapped on the canvas.

## Technical notes

Use Flutter `Shortcuts`/`Actions`/`Focus`/`FocusTraversalGroup` with an explicit `OrderedTraversalPolicy`; a global intent map centralises the shortcut table (`app/lib/a11y/shortcuts.dart`). Web landmarks/skip-links rely on Flutter web semantics (§3.1 — the weakest surface, test explicitly). Canvas object focus reads the parallel tree from {{SN-A11Y-003}}. `touch-action: none` only on the canvas element; chrome keeps page zoom (`gestures-and-shortcuts.md` §7). References `gestures-and-shortcuts.md` §6/§9 and `accessibility.md` §8. Focus-ring colour uses SN-DS-006 adjusted accent where the raw accent is low-contrast.

## Security & privacy

None beyond baseline: input routing only; never log key content or note text (CWE-532). Correct platform focus/keyboard integration: MASVS-PLATFORM-1. No egress.

## UX notes

Matches the shortcut conventions users know from Notability/Goodnotes (`gestures-and-shortcuts.md` §6). Focus rings must render >= 3:1 in every look x dark mode; where the accent is weak (Cyberpunk, Neo-Brutalism light) use the adjusted accent or `--ink` (`accessibility.md` §4.2). The cheat sheet mirrors the design's long-press-`Cmd` behaviour.

## Test plan

Widget: `app/test/a11y/keyboard_nav_test.dart` drives `Tab`/`Shift+Tab`/`Esc`/tool keys and asserts traversal order, no-trap, text-field suppression, and canvas object stepping/nudge; a web-semantics test asserts landmarks + skip links. Manual: NVDA/JAWS keyboard walk of editor + overlays; external keyboard on iPad.

## Dependencies

SN-DS-003 (focusable components), SN-ED-002 (editor + tools); reads {{SN-A11Y-003}} (object tree) for canvas navigation.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Add non-gesture and non-drag alternatives for every interaction
body:
## Context

WCAG 2.5.1 (Pointer Gestures), 2.5.7 (Dragging Movements), 2.5.2 (Pointer Cancellation) and 2.5.8 (Target Size) require that every multipoint/path gesture and every drag has a single-pointer / non-drag alternative, that actions commit on the up-event and are cancellable, and that targets meet the platform floor (`accessibility.md` §2/§9, `gestures-and-shortcuts.md` §9, PRD-CO-318/PRD-CO-319/PRD-CO-320). Motor-impaired users, switch users and many students on small phones cannot perform pinch/lasso/drag reliably. This issue guarantees the button/menu/numeric alternatives the gesture doc promises in its columns.

## Scope

**In:** zoom **buttons** (in/out/actual/fit) as the alternative to pinch-zoom; **two-finger undo** duplicated by the Undo button/shortcut; **lasso** duplicated by tap-select + a selection mode; object **move** via tap-select + arrow-nudge / numeric position; **resize** via numeric 'type-to-resize' entry as the alternative to the drag handle; **page reorder** via move-up/down buttons as the alternative to drag; **colour slider** via numeric/HEX entry; **palette dock drag** via a Settings 'Toolbar position' segmented control; ensuring strokes/gestures commit on **up-event** and are cancellable/undoable (a stroke aborted by a second finger or palm is removed, not committed); auditing interactive targets to >= 24 px (web) / >= 44 pt (iPadOS) / >= 48 dp (Android).

**Out:** keyboard traversal + shortcuts ({{SN-A11Y-008}}); Switch/Voice ({{SN-A11Y-010}}); the stabilisation/single-touch motor features ({{SN-A11Y-013}}); the underlying tool/selection implementations (owned by SN-ED-001) — this issue adds their accessible alternatives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Zoom, lasso-select, object move, object resize, page reorder, colour choice, and palette docking each have a working non-gesture / non-drag alternative reachable by tap and by keyboard.
- [ ] Object move via arrow-nudge steps by a documented increment (fine/coarse); resize accepts numeric width/height; colour accepts HEX/numeric.
- [ ] Every stroke/drag commits on the up-event and is cancellable before commit and undoable after; a palm/second-finger cancel removes the wet stroke (`pointercancel`/`FLAG_CANCELED`).
- [ ] An audit shows all toolbar/overlay targets meet the platform minimum (44 pt / 48 dp / 24 px); chips meet the floor with spacing.
- [ ] Every long-press object menu has a right-click equivalent on desktop/web.

## Technical notes

Extend the editor tool state machine (SN-ED-002) and palette dock (SN-ED-005) with alternative entry points; the dock-position control lives in Settings and drives the same dock state as the drag. Numeric entry uses accessible `SaneTextField`s. Cancellation semantics follow `gestures-and-shortcuts.md` §7 (multi-finger cancels the wet stroke). Target-size audit can reuse the `flutter_test` tap-target guideline in {{SN-A11Y-016}}. References `accessibility.md` §9 and `gestures-and-shortcuts.md` §9.

## Security & privacy

None beyond baseline: alternative input paths only; no content logging (CWE-532), no egress, no secrets. Correct pointer-cancellation avoids committing unintended strokes (data-integrity nicety). Platform integration: MASVS-PLATFORM-1.

## UX notes

Alternatives are discoverable, not hidden: zoom buttons in the page-nav cluster, reorder buttons in the page rail context menu, dock position in Settings 'Toolbar position'. Works across all looks/dark mode. Copy follows the warm voice ('Move up', 'Type a width'). Larger-target option composes with {{SN-A11Y-013}}.

## Test plan

Widget: `app/test/a11y/non_gesture_alternatives_test.dart` exercises each alternative (zoom buttons change scale, arrow-nudge moves the selection, numeric resize applies, reorder buttons reorder, HEX sets colour, dock control re-docks) and asserts up-event commit + cancellation removes the wet stroke; `app/test/a11y/target_size_test.dart` asserts platform minimums. Manual: switch-user walkthrough of move/resize/reorder.

## Dependencies

SN-ED-002 (tool state machine), SN-ED-005 (palette dock).

## Definition of done

- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, widget, golden, security scans)
- [ ] Docs/ADR updated if behaviour or architecture changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md
